title: Linux Basics
description: Foundational Linux command-line and system concepts

questions.question: Which command lists files including hidden ones?
questions.explanation: The -a flag includes entries starting with a dot (hidden files). Without it, ls skips them.

questions.question: What does `pwd` print?
questions.explanation: pwd stands for Print Working Directory — it outputs the absolute path of your current location.

questions.question: Which command moves you to your home directory regardless of where you are?
questions.explanation: ~ is a shell shorthand for $HOME. Running `cd` with no arguments also goes to $HOME.

questions.question: What does a path starting with / indicate?
questions.explanation: Paths beginning with / start from the filesystem root (top-level), making them absolute.

questions.question: Which command copies a directory recursively?
questions.explanation: cp requires -r (recursive) to copy directories. Without it, cp only works on files.

questions.question: What does `mv` do when source and destination are on the same filesystem?
questions.explanation: On the same filesystem mv is just a rename — it updates the directory entry without copying data, making it instant.

questions.question: Which command shows a real-time dynamic view of running processes?
questions.explanation: top provides an interactive, auto-refreshing view. ps gives a static snapshot.

questions.question: What signal does `kill -9` send?
questions.explanation: Signal 9 is SIGKILL — it cannot be caught or ignored by the process. Use SIGTERM (15) first for a graceful shutdown.

questions.question: What permission does `chmod 755` give to the owner?
questions.explanation: 7 in octal = rwx (4+2+1). The first digit is for the owner, so the owner gets full read/write/execute.

questions.question: Which command changes the owner of a file?
questions.explanation: chown changes the owning user (and optionally group) of a file. chgrp only changes the group.
